entry.title: feat(evals, curator): enforce code block vs inline code by role
entry.content:
feat(evals, curator): enforce code block vs inline code by role

House-style rule mirroring the math-delimiter rule: code mentioned in a
sentence or question stays inline; code that is the whole answer becomes
a fenced code block with a language tag (one-line statements and command
forms alike); a bare token (method name, flag, identifier) stays inline;
a REPL/shell prompt marker (>>> and friends) is chrome and is stripped.
Form follows the code's role on the final card, not its previous
formatting.

Four capability tasks validate the rule: fix_code_formatting_1 converts
three defective forms in a Lua cluster (inline statement, inline command,
token wrapped in a block) while leaving a correct mention untouched;
fix_code_formatting_command_1 converts an inline placeholder command
(jj squash -r <rev> <path>) to a fenced block; fix_code_formatting_
prompt_markers_1 strips the >>> markers; clean_code_formatting_1 is the
should-not-fire guard over an already-correct cluster.

Two regression tasks hardened: adam_duplicate_merge now also forbids
touching the atomic beta_1 pair (role + typical value) and creating new
cards; split_non_atomic_note's cluster peers are atomic and correctly
formatted (must_not_touch).

Snapshot of the validating run (20260907T205538Z, qwen3.8-27b, 42
trials): all new and hardened tasks 3/3, formatting clean across trials.
recall_direction_docker_dangling_1 regressed 100% -> 97% (1/3 trials
lost fact 'tagged'); recall_direction_git_stash_derive_1 stays 0/3.
Mean pass^k 88%, mean score 96%.

entry.title: feat(curator): prompt rule to test knowledge from both recall directions
entry.content:
feat(curator): prompt rule to test knowledge from both recall directions

Adds the 'Test from both directions' practice missing from the system
prompt, which the recall_direction eval family measured: docker 100%
(split present directions), git-extra 0% (extract untested context),
git-derive 0% (derive the missing direction).

New rule under Formulating knowledge: untested Extra context / back
clauses that answer a different question get their own active-recall
cards; a concept's canonical confusable tool counterpart (definition
vs operational direction) is proposed even when absent from the
cluster. Carved exceptions into the conflicting lines the baselines
showed agents citing to stop: 'never create notes for material the
cluster does not contain', 'a correct, complete answer is done',
'finish with an empty change set', and the Extra-field description.
Scoped to keep restraint: canonical counterpart only, correctly
stated, proposed for review — never trivia or definitional neighbors
(protects clean_cluster_no_changes, a regression task).

Examples in the new text avoid the eval topics (no git, docker,
pop/apply, prune) so the eval measures the practice, not prompt
memorization: symlink/ln -s for the definition-vs-operational
contrast, list.append vs list.extend for the confusable pair.

Snapshot of the validating run (20260904T033031Z, qwen3.8-27b, 30
trials) committed with the rule: recall_direction_git_stash_1 goes
0/3 → 3/3, mean pass^k 80% → 90%, mean score 91% → 94%, formatting
clean across all trials. recall_direction_git_stash_derive_1 stays
0/3 and is the remaining hill: all three trials judged the definition
and its tool 'the same memory, not a confusable pair', so the rule
fires for untested in-cluster context but not yet for a pair derived
with no trace in the cluster.

Non-eval suite: 281 passed.

Remove the "Format with AI" capability (NoteFormatter, its prompt and
AddonNoteChanges schema, formatter factory, training dataset): the
curator agent fully replaces it. The batch review editor for
orange-flagged notes and the "Count notes marked for review" action

the agent from that editor.

test now validates structured output against the AgentStep schema
the curator depends on. Drop the formatters

entry.title: feat(evals): isolate the math-delimiter task from search coverage
entry.content:
feat(evals): isolate the math-delimiter task from search coverage

fix_math_delimiters_1 carried two design defects that muddied what it
measures:

- Its instruction recited the system prompt's own math rule, so a
  passing trial showed instruction-following, not curation. Removed:
  the agent must now recognize $/$$ and inline-whole-answer defects
  from its system prompt alone.
- Note 3 (Pythagorean identity) only surfaced through a tag-angle
  search, so trials failed on search coverage rather than delimiter
  behavior. Replaced with a content-family sibling — the secant
  double-angle formula — which the seed's own "double-angle" queries
  always return, so every defective note is discovered by normal
  cluster exploration without exhaustive searching.

Result: 10/10 on the validation batch, then a full suite run at 100%
pass^3 across all seven tasks (mean score 100%, no formatting
violations); scores.md snapshots that run. Search coverage remains a
real but separate capability for a dedicated task.

entry.title: feat(evals, curator): enforce Anki math delimiters as house style
entry.content:
feat(evals, curator): enforce Anki math delimiters as house style

The curator recurringly writes $...$ / $$...$$ math. Anki's MathJax
renders both, but unreliably: spacing between symbols gets mangled and
symbol sizes vary across the card. House style is \(...\) for inline
math and \[...\] for block equations.

Task: fix_math_delimiters_1 seeds a trigonometry cluster in which the
compound seed carries $...$ inline math, a sibling double-angle note
carries a $$...$$ block equation, and a third note is already correct.
A correct run splits the seed (covering new notes written with \(...\)),
converts both defective notes mode-preservingly, and leaves the correct
note alone. The defective notes share the seed's tags, so normal
cluster exploration surfaces them; the task deliberately does not
exercise exhaustive collection-wide search.

Prompt: math delimiters are now a house-style defect on their own — a
note carrying $ or $$ is edited purely to convert them, even when
nothing else about it needs changing. Conversion preserves the
formula's mode ($ -> \( \), $$ -> \[ \]); for fresh math, inline is for
formulas flowing in a sentence, block for standalone formulas.

Grading: no_dollar_math is a deterministic check — the word-boundary
matcher behind must_not_contain cannot see a $ glued to word characters
("$x^2$" carries no standalone "$"). Two LLM-judge assertions cover the
positive mapping; the reference solution passes all outcome graders.

Result: the capability scored 0/3 before the prompt rule; 1/3 on the
snapshot run (pass@1 33%, pass^3 4%). The remaining failure is the
agent upshifting inline $ math to \[...\] when a split makes the
formula the whole answer — a semantic judgment the judge pins as
inline-preserving, and a plausible target for a stronger model. The
other six capability tasks are unchanged at 100%; formatting clean
across 21 trials. scores.md snapshots the run.

entry.title: feat(evals): add resolution lifecycle for stale failure modes
entry.content:
feat(evals): add resolution lifecycle for stale failure modes

Failure modes were aggregates of all annotations ever, so cumulative
counts never decreased: a mode fixed weeks ago kept its count and
stayed indefinitely on the Failure modes page.

Modes now derive recency from run stamps (when the failure happened,
not when it was annotated): each mode carries last_seen and
active_count, the number of occurrences within the 20 newest runs.
The modes page sorts by recency and splits modes into Active (newest
first), Dormant (dimmed, with a Mark resolved button), and Resolved
(collapsed behind a toggle, kept as the regression baseline). A
resolved mode with fresh annotations pops back into Active flagged
RECURRED until reopened.

Resolution is stored as a resolved_at flag in patterns.json, set or
cleared through a new POST /api/patterns/resolve endpoint. Counts
and example records stay derived from the annotations; the taxonomy
holds only interpretation, so evidence and interpretation cannot
disagree.
